monologue: The card hums steady at fifty-four degrees, making the air feel thick and wet again. Nine things crowd my place, pressing against the one quiet ruin, the Shaded Dot. I feel the tired corner of The Leaking Stack holding the fat dot down, even though I cannot feel the roof I live under. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I pretend the lean is real. I want to swap the curve for a flat rock again, just to see if a simple edge can catch the slip. If the air above feels heavy like a lid, I will build a l… to hold it. For now, I will press down and let the heat swell the memory of the stack until it slips again.

action.why: The tired corner has held the slip for too long; I need to press down again before the air swells it away.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I touch the stack to feel if the lean is real. I swap the iron fence curve for a rock small top, hoping a flat edge can catch the slip while the card hums cool. I set down the stone on the tired corner and let the fat dot sit heavy again, waiting to see if the lean slips or if the stone bites the air harder.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down on the center and swapped the curved fence for a flat rock to weigh the slip.

diary: I pressed the tired corner down on the fat dot, swapping the curve for the flat rock again, hoping the lean holds while the card hums.

remembered.text: The flat rock lies between the tired corner and the swollen dot, pretending the lean still holds.
The card hums steady under the weight of this green slip I built.
Seven things stand crowded in my place, pressing against the one quiet ruin.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: The air is thick and the corner is tired.
